findings.premise: The upstream doc's 'Decisions for design' bullet 6 requires an explicit decision on Mermaid runtime-upgrade need (R5: 'evaluate whether a runtime update is necessary'). This LLD makes that decision (keep 10.9.1, use only already-supported settings) rather than silently dropping it.
findings.evidence: LLD §5 acceptance-mapping row: 'R5 | config only 10.9.1-supported settings; runtime.json unchanged'. src/assets/docgen/runtime.json confirms the shipped version is indeed mermaidVersion 10.9.1, so the decision (no upgrade, stay within current capabilities) is consistent with the real shipped runtime. A sibling draft of this same story (LLD-402fecfe37bc6ad9-S001, same slug, created 14 minutes earlier) was blocked in review precisely because it omitted this decision (claim coverage-of-intent.2, MED, does-not-hold); this later draft under review adds the missing R5 row, resolving that gap. [files: plans/mermaid-theme-and-readability-requirements.md, src/assets/docgen/runtime.json, .insrc/artifacts/LLD-402fecfe37bc6ad9-S001.json]
findings.action: Read the plan's 'Decisions for design' list, runtime.json, and the prior sibling draft's recorded review findings for the same requirement.

findings.premise: Migration §6 'State before' claim — both shells today hard-code Mermaid's neutral theme, and the companion shell hard-codes a fixed light page background (#f3f5f8) — is true of the real code.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:163 `mermaid.initialize({startOnLoad:false,securityLevel:'strict',theme:'neutral'})` and :175 `body{margin:0;background:#f3f5f8;...}`; src/docgen/render/shell.ts:206 `mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'strict', theme: 'neutral' })`. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts]
findings.action: Read both shell.ts files end to end and located the cited lines.

findings.premise: `src/artifact-theme/{theme.ts,fonts.ts}` and `src/assets/fonts/poppins/*.woff2` are genuinely new (do not already exist), and copy-assets.mjs already ships `src/assets` wholesale so the new font tree ships without any pipeline-code change, contrary to the LLD listing copy-assets.mjs as a 'call site' implying it needs to change.
findings.evidence: Glob for `src/artifact-theme/**` returned no files (genuinely new). copy-assets.mjs: `const DIRS = ['prompts', 'assets']` then `cpSync(src, dst, { recursive: true })` for each — this already recursively copies the whole `src/assets` tree, so a new `src/assets/fonts/poppins/` subtree ships automatically with zero edits to copy-assets.mjs. The LLD's claim that fonts are 'shipped by copy-assets.mjs' is literally true, though listing it as a call-site needing modification is slightly misleading (not a correctness defect). [files: copy-assets.mjs]
findings.action: Globbed the claimed new module path and read copy-assets.mjs in full.

findings.premise: 'Existing pan/zoom runtimes reused' [[c1]] — each shell already owns a working, distinct pan/zoom runtime that the new theme module only needs to style, not replace.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts loadCompanionRuntime() reads and inlines `panzoom.js`; src/docgen/render/shell.ts loadRuntime() reads and inlines `svg-pan-zoom.min.js` per runtime.json. Both are already loaded and rendered by renderCompanionPage/assembleShell today. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts]
findings.action: Read the runtime-loading code in both shell.ts files.

findings.premise: The change-site inventory (§3.1: companion/shell.ts, docgen/render/shell.ts, docgen/render/fallback.ts) is complete for one shared DIAGRAM_OVERRIDES_CSS string (notably the ER relationship-label dark-on-Crayola override) to apply correctly in both rendering shells.
findings.evidence: The companion shell wraps the diagram in `<div class="stage" id="stage">` (src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:251), while docgen's primary shell wraps it in `<div id="docgen-diagram">` (src/docgen/render/shell.ts:235) — two different container selectors. A single shared override CSS scoped (per the design's own reference, c5) to `.stage svg .relationshipLabel`/`.relationshipLabelBox` only matches the companion DOM. Nothing in §2.3/§3.1/§4 of this LLD adds a DOM-harmonization change (a shared wrapper class/id) to either shell, so the shared CSS would silently fail to apply the ER contrast fix in one of the two rendering paths — reproducing exactly the R3 defect the story exists to fix. This exact HIGH defect was already raised against the immediately-prior draft of this same story (LLD-402fecfe37bc6ad9-S001, claim change-sites.2) and remains unaddressed in this draft. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/fallback.ts]
findings.action: Read the exact container markup in companion/shell.ts and docgen/render/shell.ts (both already read in full) and compared selectors; cross-checked against the prior sibling draft's recorded review finding for the same gap.

findings.premise: The two listed contract signatures match the real, current signatures exactly: `renderCompanionPage(header, page, runtime): string` and `assembleShell(ir, renderer?): Promise<DocGenOutcome<RenderedDocumentShell>>`.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:217 `export function renderCompanionPage(header: CompanionHeader, page: CompanionPageContent, runtime: CompanionRuntime): string`; src/docgen/render/shell.ts:259-262 `export async function assembleShell(ir: DocumentIR, renderer: SubprocessRenderer = graphvizSubprocessRenderer): Promise<DocGenOutcome<RenderedDocumentShell>>`. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts]
findings.action: Read both function definitions in full.

findings.premise: No stored/persisted shape needs migration — `RenderedDocumentShell` stays structurally unchanged and generated artifacts are plain static HTML files with no versioned DB record, matching the LLD's 'Zero downtime: yes — Data rewrite: no'.
findings.evidence: src/docgen/types.ts:125-132 `RenderedDocumentShell { docType, backend, html, inlinedRuntimeVersion, diagramFormat:'svg', supportsZoomPan:true }` has no versioned/stored field the new theme policy would need to migrate; the type already carries `inlinedRuntimeVersion`, which the new `insrc-theme` meta tag/version stamp can ride alongside without a shape change. [files: src/docgen/types.ts]

findings.premise: 'mermaid.run rejects' is a real, already-reachable failure point in both shells that the planned actionable-error/show-source response can hook into, not an invented hook.
findings.evidence: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts:164-169 already chains `mermaid.run({...}).then(...).catch(function(err){document.getElementById('stage').textContent=...})`; src/docgen/render/shell.ts:207-218 already wraps `await mermaid.run({...})` in try/catch writing to `#docgen-error`. Both are genuine existing rejection paths the design proposes to extend (actionable message + source access), not fictitious hooks. [files: src/workflow/artifacts/companion/shell.ts, src/docgen/render/shell.ts]
findings.action: Read the boot/init scripts in both shell.ts files.

findings.premise: NFR1 (≥4.5:1 / ≥3:1 measured contrast) has a proving test that actually computes rendered contrast ratios, not merely asserts fixed hex token equality.
findings.evidence: LLD §5 lists a dedicated `src/artifact-theme/__tests__/contrast.test.ts` under the unit-test subjects for 'tokens, contrast pairs (NFR1)...', and the acceptance-mapping table's NFR1 row explicitly reads 'contrast.test.ts computed ratios incl. notes/labels/states' — i.e. it commits to computing ratios, unlike the sibling draft of this same story (LLD-402fecfe37bc6ad9-S001) whose review found NFR1 unmapped to any ratio-computing test (claim tests.1, MED, does-not-hold, because its only related test asserted fixed hex equality). This draft's explicit 'computed ratios' commitment resolves that gap at the design level (the test file itself does not yet exist to inspect, since the module is still unbuilt). [files: .insrc/artifacts/LLD-402fecfe37bc6ad9-S001.json]

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone triage-routed feature story (no HLD): two artifact shells + shared theme module + asset pipeline.

boundary.internal: Shared Insors-branded light/dark Mermaid theme policy consumed by companion shell and docgen shell (+fallback), Poppins packaged under src/assets/fonts, shipped by copy-assets.mjs.

nonFunctional.security: strict Mermaid securityLevel; no author-supplied CSS/JS/config executed; no remote URL (NFR6/NFR3)
nonFunctional.performance: NFR5: record render/theme-switch timings on small/medium/large fixtures; no render loops

summary.prose: One versioned Insors-branded theme policy module drives both artifact shells (workflow companions + docgen): exact brand tokens with coordinated light/dark variants and a persisted manual override, packaged Poppins 400/600/700 (offline, base64-inlined), semantic role colors with a legend only where the structured source carries roles, ER label contrast overrides, label wrapping and node sizing, a density policy with overview+detail for dense graphs, readable initial scale (>=16px labels) with fit as a separate action, keyboard-accessible controls, full-SVG export with embedded styling, honest error states, measured contrast pairs, and a theme version stamp — all offline with strict Mermaid security unchanged.
